title: 3-4. WE HAVE COME TO LIVE HERE AWHILE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh asked the brothers, 'What is your occupation?' 'Your servants are shepherds,' they replied to Pharaoh, 'just as our fathers were.' They also said to him, 'We have come to live here for a while, because the famine is severe in Canaan and your servants' flocks have no pasture. So now, please let your servants settle in Goshen.'" — Gen 47:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The brothers answer honestly. They are shepherds, as their fathers were — the very occupation Egyptians despised. No dressing it up, no attempt to sound more impressive than they are.

But look at the phrase they use about their stay: "We have come to live here for a while." They are not claiming Egypt. They are asking for temporary shelter. In their own minds, they belong somewhere else.

That instinct is worth holding onto. Israel would remain in Egypt for four hundred years, and over time many of them would forget they were only passing through. Comfort has a way of turning a temporary stay into a permanent home.

Scripture says believers are foreigners and strangers on earth, people looking for a better country (Heb 11:13-16; 1 Pet 2:11). This does not mean we despise this life or refuse to enjoy it. It means we hold it the way you hold accommodation you are staying in for a season — gratefully, but loosely.

Ask yourself honestly: does your life look like someone settling permanently here, or like someone who knows they are heading home?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though this world is your permanent home?
2. Where has comfort quietly become more of an anchor than you intended?
3. What would it look like to hold your circumstances more loosely this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me live gratefully in this world without sinking my roots so deep that I forget I am heading home to You. Keep my heart set on the better country. Amen.
